# Josephine Barry

## Appearance

Josephine Barry is an old woman who is thin, prim, and rigid in her appearance. She has a wrinkled cheek and sharp, twinkling black eyes that remain bright and undimmed.

_Sources: [v1 CHAPTER XIX. A Concert, a Catastrophe, and a Confession P77](../source/v01-c19.md#nw-v01-c19-p0077), [v1 CHAPTER XXIX. An Epoch in Anne’s Life P17](../source/v01-c29.md#nw-v01-c29-p0017), [v1 CHAPTER XXIX. An Epoch in Anne’s Life P31](../source/v01-c29.md#nw-v01-c29-p0031), [v1 CHAPTER XXXV. The Winter at Queen’s P8](../source/v01-c35.md#nw-v01-c35-p0008)_

## Personality

Josephine Barry is a notably selfish older woman who generally prioritizes herself over others. She is also characterized as extremely prim and proper, with a tendency to scold severely.

_Sources: [v1 CHAPTER XIX. A Concert, a Catastrophe, and a Confession P54](../source/v01-c19.md#nw-v01-c19-p0054), [v1 CHAPTER XXIX. An Epoch in Anne’s Life P31](../source/v01-c29.md#nw-v01-c29-p0031)_

## History

Josephine Barry, an aunt who resided in [Charlottetown](../codex/places.md#charlottetown), visited [Orchard Slope](../codex/places.md#orchard-slope) and was startled when [Anne](../character/anne-shirley.md) and [Diana](../character/diana-barry.md) jumped onto her bed late at night. Furious, she initially threatened to cancel Diana's music lessons, but after [Anne](../character/anne-shirley.md) arrived to personally confess and explain the situation, Josephine was amused and forgave them. The two became close friends, and Josephine stayed in [Avonlea](../codex/places.md#avonlea) and invited [Anne](../character/anne-shirley.md) to visit her in the city.

_Sources: [v1 CHAPTER XIX. A Concert, a Catastrophe, and a Confession P27](../source/v01-c19.md#nw-v01-c19-p0027), [v1 CHAPTER XIX. ## Quotes

> "I dare say your claim to sympathy is just as strong as mine. It all depends on the way we look at it. Sit down here and tell me about yourself."
>
> — Josephine Barry — [v1 CHAPTER XIX. A Concert, a Catastrophe, and a Confession P88](../source/v01-c19.md#nw-v01-c19-p0088)

> "Remember, you Anne-girl, when you come to town you’re to visit me and I’ll put you in my very sparest spare-room bed to sleep."
>
> — Josephine Barry — [v1 CHAPTER XIX. A Concert, a Catastrophe, and a Confession P96](../source/v01-c19.md#nw-v01-c19-p0096)

> "Oh, I must, hey? I rather think Diana did her share of the jumping at least. Such carryings on in a respectable house!"
>
> — Josephine Barry — [v1 CHAPTER XIX. A Concert, a Catastrophe, and a Confession P82](../source/v01-c19.md#nw-v01-c19-p0082)

> "She amuses me, and at my time of life an amusing person is a rarity."
>
> — Josephine Barry — [v1 CHAPTER XIX. A Concert, a Catastrophe, and a Confession P92](../source/v01-c19.md#nw-v01-c19-p0092)

> "I’ve made up my mind to stay simply for the sake of getting better acquainted with that Anne-girl,"
>
> — Josephine Barry — [v1 CHAPTER XIX. A Concert, a Catastrophe, and a Confession P92](../source/v01-c19.md#nw-v01-c19-p0092)

## Relationships

### [Anne Shirley](../character/anne-shirley.md) · [the relationship](../relationships/anne-shirley--josephine-barry.md)

Josephine Barry and [Anne Shirley](../character/anne-shirley.md) are firm friends who frequently visit and amuse one another. They first met when [Anne](../character/anne-shirley.md) accidentally jumped on Josephine while she was sleeping in a spare bed at Diana's house. After [Anne](../character/anne-shirley.md) personally confessed and explained the situation to her, Josephine was charmed by her honesty, chose to forgive the mistake, and established a close bond with her.

_Sources: [v1 CHAPTER XIX. A Concert, a Catastrophe, and a Confession P27](../source/v01-c19.md#nw-v01-c19-p0027), [v1 CHAPTER XIX.
